apply_mutations.summary: Apply a batch atomically under one new revision (I31).
apply_mutations.text:
Apply a batch atomically under one new revision (I31).

Handler: `rocket_engine.project.service.ProjectService.apply_mutations`.

Every mutation is validated before anything lands: any
failure names its document and leaves the revision, the
files, and the log untouched. Only a fully valid batch at
the live head advances once and appends a single
mutations_applied event.

Arguments:

- `mutations` (required): Non-empty list of {op, path, content?} mappings; op is write (needs text content) or delete (takes none).
- `expected_revision`: Revision the writer read.

Returns:

Mutation mapping with revision transition, new head, actor, joined diff summary, rewind handle, the single appended event, per-mutation results, cursor, and request id.

Raises:

ProjectError: request_conflict for a reused id with new text; invalid_command for a malformed batch (names the document when one is addressable); invalid_path or path_escape for a bad path; unknown_document for a delete of a missing document; revision_conflict for a stale head; invalid_ledger when a durable write fails (best effort rollback already attempted).

Caution: All-or-nothing means one revision for the whole batch — a half-landed batch is a bug, never a state.

create_project.summary: Create one managed project at revision p12.
create_project.text:
Create one managed project at revision p12.

Handler: `rocket_engine.project.service.ProjectService.create_project`.

The new ledger starts clean (no events); the response still
carries the approval-UI fields with a None prior revision.
Idempotent replays return the stored response instead of
failing as duplicates.

Arguments:

- `new_project_id` (required): Slug for the project to create.

Returns:

Creation mapping with the new project id, p12 head, actor, diff summary, revision transition, rewind handle, empty events, and request id.

Raises:

ProjectError: invalid_command without an engine root; invalid_project for a non-slug id; project_exists for a duplicate; request_conflict for a reused id with new text; invalid_ledger when the project dir cannot be written.

Caution: Creating the bound project itself is a duplicate once its dir exists — create-then-list, never assume.

delete_doc.summary: Delete one document: gate, remove, advance, log.
delete_doc.text:
Delete one document: gate, remove, advance, log.

Caution: Deleting advances the revision like any mutation — stale writers fail instead of merging.

rewind.summary: Restore managed bytes to a prior revision under a new head.
rewind.text:
Restore managed bytes to a prior revision under a new head.

Handler: `rocket_engine.project.service.ProjectService.rewind`.

The target snapshot replaces every managed document
byte-identically; runs, the ledger, and the snapshots
themselves are left alone. History stays append-only: the
restore advances from the live head and appends a single
`project_rewound` event recording the target. Linked caller
trees are never written — files outside `.rocket/` are
listed in the response as left untouched.

Arguments:

- `target_revision` (required): Snapshot revision to restore.
- `expected_revision`: Revision the writer read.

Returns:

Mutation mapping with revision transition, target revision, new head, actor, diff summary, external-file report, rewind handle, the appended event, cursor, and request id.

Raises:

ProjectError: request_conflict for a reused id with new text; invalid_command for a missing target or a target that equals the live head; unknown_revision for a revision with no snapshot; revision_conflict for a stale head; invalid_ledger when the durable restore fails (best-effort rollback already attempted).

Caution: Rewinding advances — the new head is not the target id, and stale writers fail instead of merging. Caller files outside `.rocket/` are reported, never touched.

run_drc.summary: run_drc via Magic: batch DRC over .mag cells, lambda-unit boxes.
run_drc.text:
run_drc via Magic: batch DRC over .mag cells, lambda-unit boxes.

Tools: `magic` (default), `klayout` — `deck.tool` selects; a missing tool falls back to the default, an unknown tool fails `unsupported_operation` before anything runs.

Handlers: `rocket_engine.adapters.drc.MagicDrcAdapter`, `rocket_engine.adapters.drc_kl.KlayoutDrcAdapter`.

#### Tool `magic`

run_drc via Magic: batch DRC over .mag cells, lambda-unit boxes.

Serves the run_drc operation with deck.tool `magic` (the
operation default). Tcl over stdin against a loaded cell; the
result is {total, violations[]} with rule/message plus
lambda-unit bbox areas.

Arguments:

- `cell` (required): Cell name loaded inside magic.
- `cell_file` (required): Path to the .mag cell file.
- `tech`: Magic tech name (default scmos).
- `deck`: Optional mapping; deck.tool selects the solver (magic here, klayout for the KLayout path).
- `workdir`: Run directory (default ".").
- `expected_revision`: Revision the writer read; defaults to the command's own expected_revision entry.

Returns:

{total, violations[]} with rule plus lambda-unit bbox areas.

Raises:

(preflight) AdapterError: unsupported_operation for another operation, missing_dependency for a missing magic binary or unloadable tech, invalid_reference for a missing cell file.

(execute) AdapterError: missing_dependency when the tech fails to load mid-run, runner_unavailable when magic output carries no DRC total line, plus the preflight codes (execute re-checks first).

(parse) AdapterError: runner_unavailable when the output has no DRC total line.

Caution: Magic exits 0 even for broken cells and unknown techs — the verdict always comes from parsed output, never the exit code. Timeout is fixed at 120 s.

#### Tool `klayout`

run_drc via KLayout: synthetic checks or foundry .lydrc decks.

Serves the run_drc operation with deck.tool `klayout`. Two
modes: synthetic width/space checks over one layer from
`rules`, or a foundry .lydrc deck over `gds_file` with
violations parsed from the report database. Locations are
metric bbox_um.

Arguments:

- `gds_file` (required): GDS layout under check.
- `rules`: Synthetic check {layer [l, d], width_um, space_um, name?} — one check form is required (rules or a deck file).
- `deck_file`: Foundry .lydrc deck path (deck mode).
- `deck`: Optional mapping; deck.tool selects the solver (klayout here), deck.path/deck_file/file names the deck in deck mode.
- `workdir`: Run directory (default ".").
- `expected_revision`: Revision the writer read; defaults to the command's own expected_revision entry.

Returns:

{total, violations[]} with rule, message, and metric bbox_um where the deck reports geometry.

Raises:

(preflight) AdapterError: unsupported_operation for another operation, missing_dependency for a missing klayout binary, invalid_reference for a missing GDS or deck file, invalid_command for a malformed rules mapping.

(execute) AdapterError: invalid_reference for a missing workdir, runner_unavailable when klayout produces no report, plus the preflight codes (execute re-checks first).

(parse) AdapterError: runner_unavailable when the deck run has no report, the report is not valid XML, or the synthetic output has no TOTAL line.

Caution: KLayout exits 0 regardless — the verdict always comes from parsed output, never the exit code.

run_extraction.text:
run_extraction via Magic: .mag cells to .ext/.spice netlists.

Tools: `magic` (default) — `deck.tool` selects; a missing tool falls back to the default, an unknown tool fails `unsupported_operation` before anything runs.

Handlers: `rocket_engine.adapters.extract_magic.MagicExtractAdapter`.

#### Tool `magic`

run_extraction via Magic: .mag cells to .ext/.spice netlists.

Serves the run_extraction operation with deck.tool `magic` (the
only tool). Loads the cell, extracts all, and converts with
ext2spice; the result carries the netlist artifact paths plus
device counts.

Arguments:

- `cell` (required): Cell name loaded and extracted.
- `cell_file` (required): Path to the .mag cell file.
- `tech` (required): Magic tech name — one tech form is required (tech, tech_file, or deck.path/tech_file/file).
- `tech_file`: Magic tech file path (a hash-checked store deck by the caller).
- `deck`: Optional mapping naming the tech file (deck.path/tech_file/file).
- `workdir`: Run directory (default ".").
- `expected_revision`: Revision the writer read; defaults to the command's own expected_revision entry.

Returns:

Result with cell, artifact paths, device_count, devices, and no violations.

Raises:

(preflight) AdapterError: unsupported_operation for another operation, invalid_command for a missing cell, a Tcl-unsafe cell name, or no tech form, missing_dependency for a missing magic binary or unloadable tech, invalid_reference for a missing cell or tech file.

(execute) AdapterError: invalid_reference for a missing workdir, missing_dependency when the tech fails to load mid-run, runner_unavailable when the output has no ext2spice marker or no .ext/.spice pair, plus the preflight codes (execute re-checks first).

(parse) AdapterError: runner_unavailable when the output has no ext2spice marker, no spice text, or no subckt block.

Caution: Magic exits 0 even for broken cells — the verdict always comes from parsed output, never the exit code.

(execute) AdapterError: invalid_reference for a missing workdir, runner_unavailable on a sim timeout, plus the preflight codes (execute re-checks first).

(parse) AdapterError: runner_unavailable when a compiled run has no run block.

Caution: $error exits 0 and hangs raise instead of hanging the engine — the verdict always comes from parsed output, never the exit code alone.

run_lvs.summary: run_lvs via Netgen: layout vs schematic, TOP-level compare.
run_lvs.text:
run_lvs via Netgen: layout vs schematic, TOP-level compare.

Tools: `netgen` (default) — `deck.tool` selects; a missing tool falls back to the default, an unknown tool fails `unsupported_operation` before anything runs.

Handlers: `rocket_engine.adapters.lvs_netgen.NetgenLvsAdapter`.

#### Tool `netgen`

run_lvs via Netgen: layout vs schematic, TOP-level compare.

Serves the run_lvs operation with deck.tool `netgen` (the only
tool). Both netlists flatten to top level first (a library file
needs `cell` to select its block), then the one-shot batch LVS
runs; the result is {match, total, violations[]} with net and
device mismatches.

Arguments:

- `layout_spice` (required): Layout netlist path.
- `schematic_spice` (required): Schematic netlist path.
- `setup_file` (required): Netgen setup path — one setup form is required (setup_file or deck.path/setup_file/setup/ file).
- `deck`: Optional mapping naming the setup file (see above).
- `cell`: .subckt block to select from library netlists.
- `workdir`: Run directory (default ".").
- `expected_revision`: Revision the writer read; defaults to the command's own expected_revision entry.

Returns:

{match, total, violations[]} with lvs_net_mismatch and lvs_device_mismatch rules.

Raises:

(preflight) AdapterError: unsupported_operation for another operation, missing_dependency for a missing netgen or a banner-rejected impostor, invalid_reference for missing netlist files, invalid_command when no setup form is given.

(execute) AdapterError: invalid_reference for a missing workdir, invalid_command for an ambiguous library without cell, runner_unavailable when netgen produces no report, plus the preflight codes (execute re-checks first).

(parse) AdapterError: runner_unavailable when the output has no LVS verdict.

Caution: Netgen exits 0 on match and mismatch alike — the verdict always comes from parsed output, never the exit code. PATH presence is not enough: same-named impostor binaries are rejected by banner probe.

run_optical.summary: run_optical via SAX: frequency-domain photonic circuit sim.
run_optical.text:
run_optical via SAX: frequency-domain photonic circuit sim.

Tools: `sax` (default) — `deck.tool` selects; a missing tool falls back to the default, an unknown tool fails `unsupported_operation` before anything runs.

Handlers: `rocket_engine.adapters.sax.SaxAdapter`.

#### Tool `sax`

run_optical via SAX: frequency-domain photonic circuit sim.

Serves the run_optical operation with deck.tool `sax` (the only
tool). Stages the sim driver plus a job JSON, runs it under a
timeout, and parses the JSON envelope: spectra plus per-target
transmission measurements against min_db/max_db bounds.

Arguments:

- `sources` (required): Exactly one circuit spec YAML path.
- `timeout_s`: Sim budget in seconds (default 120).
- `tool_dir`: Directory holding the sim python; the engine interpreter otherwise.
- `deck`: Optional mapping; deck.tool must be sax here.
- `workdir`: Run directory (default ".").
- `expected_revision`: Revision the writer read; defaults to the command's own expected_revision entry.

Returns:

{total, violations[], measurements[], spectra[], sax_version} with dB values and margins.

Raises:

(preflight) AdapterError: unsupported_operation for another operation, invalid_command for a bad timeout or circuit spec, invalid_reference unless exactly one readable spec source is given, missing_dependency for an unresolvable sim python.

(execute) AdapterError: invalid_reference for a missing workdir, runner_unavailable on a sim timeout, plus the preflight codes (execute re-checks first).

(parse) AdapterError: missing_dependency when the sim python has no sax, runner_unavailable when the driver printed no JSON envelope, no result, or misses a target pair.

Caution: Missed target bounds are FAIL and a malformed circuit synthesizes an error violation with file/line — the verdict always comes from parsed output, never the exit code.

run_spice.summary: run_spice via ngspice: corner sims with measured bounds.
run_spice.text:
run_spice via ngspice: corner sims with measured bounds.

Tools: `ngspice` (default) — `deck.tool` selects; a missing tool falls back to the default, an unknown tool fails `unsupported_operation` before anything runs.

Handlers: `rocket_engine.adapters.ngspice.NgspiceAdapter`.

#### Tool `ngspice`

run_spice via ngspice: corner sims with measured bounds.

Serves the run_spice operation with deck.tool `ngspice` (the
only tool). Stages a corner deck (preamble + netlist bodies +
generated .control), runs it in batch, and parses meas_* values
against min/max bounds; bound misses are FAIL, valueless sims
synthesize sim_fail violations.

Arguments:

- `sources` (required): Netlist source paths staged as bodies.
- `measurements` (required): [{name, expr, unit?, min?, max?}] with numeric min and/or max each.
- `analyses`: .control analysis lines (default op).
- `options`: .option lines (default [wnflag=1]).
- `params`: .param name/value mapping.
- `corner`: Model corner (default tt).
- `temp_c`: Temperature in C (default 27).
- `title`: Deck title line.
- `pdk`: {id, revision, model_rel?, engine_root?} pin for PDK models via the store; omitted sims model-free.
- `timeout_s`: Sim budget in seconds (default 120).
- `tool_dir`: Directory holding ngspice; PATH otherwise.
- `deck`: Optional mapping; deck.tool must be ngspice here.
- `workdir`: Run directory (default ".").
- `expected_revision`: Revision the writer read; defaults to the command's own expected_revision entry.

Returns:

{total, violations[], measurements[]} with value, unit, target, margin, and status per measurement.

Raises:

(preflight) AdapterError: unsupported_operation for another operation, invalid_command for bad inputs (timeout, measurements, analyses, options, params, corner, temp_c, title), invalid_reference for missing sources, store codes (unknown_pdk, pdk_drift, ...) for a bad PDK pin, missing_dependency for an unresolvable ngspice.

(execute) AdapterError: invalid_reference for a missing workdir or unreadable netlist, runner_unavailable on a sim timeout, plus the preflight codes (execute re-checks first).

(parse) AdapterError: runner_unavailable when ngspice produced no output at all.

Caution: Verdicts always come from parsed output, never the exit code — and PDK models resolve through the store, so a wrong revision or tampered model fails loudly instead of simming against substitutes.

write_doc.summary: Write one document: gate, store, advance, log.
write_doc.text:
Write one document: gate, store, advance, log.

Handler: `rocket_engine.project.service.ProjectService.write_doc`.

A resubmitted envelope returns its stored response without
advancing; a new envelope gates its expected_revision, and
only an accepted write advances the revision and appends
the doc_written event.

Arguments:

- `path` (required): Document path to create or overwrite.
- `content` (required): UTF-8 text to store (1 MB limit).
- `expected_revision`: Revision the writer read.

Returns:

Mutation mapping with path, revision transition, new head, actor, diff summary, rewind handle, the appended event, cursor, and request id.

Raises:

ProjectError: request_conflict for a reused id with new text; invalid_path or path_escape for a bad path; invalid_command for non-text or oversize content or a directory path; revision_conflict for a stale head; invalid_ledger when the durable write fails.

Caution: Every accepted write advances the revision — a second writer at the old head fails instead of merging.
